author: Ivan Ball-llovera
name: MMCA modular monolith (DDD + CQRS + Aspire)
description: A complete modular-monolith solution on the MMCA.Common framework: one business module across all five layers, a REST API host, a Blazor Server + MudBlazor UI host, an Aspire AppHost, a per-database migrations project, and domain + application + architecture-fitness test projects. Shape the sample module with --flat (no child collection), --no-status (no status axis), --no-description (no description property), --no-owner (no requester/owner property), and --child (rename the child entity); name its vocabulary with --title (the aggregate's main text property) and --event-verb (the creation integration event's verb). Pick the shape of the solution itself with --database sqlserver|sqlite and --no-aspire, which compose: --database sqlite --no-aspire is a two-host app with a single database file and no container anywhere. Build the monolith now, extract a module into its own service later.

appNameUnderscores.description: Underscore form of the app name. Aspire generates a Projects.<Underscored_Project_Name> type per referenced project, so the AppHost needs this form.

appShortName.description: Last dotted segment of the app name (Contoso.Support -> Support). Names the architecture map, the typed API client, and the Aspire database resource.

appShortNameLower.description: Lower-case short name: the Aspire resource id and the default JWT audience.

appShortNameUpper.description: Upper-case short name: the design-time connection-string environment variable.

module.description: Name of the first business module, plural PascalCase (for example Orders, Billing, Reservations).

moduleLower.description: Lower-case module name: routes, the Aspire database name, and the data-source key.

moduleUpper.description: Upper-case module name: the design-time connection-string environment variable.

aggregate.description: Name of the module's aggregate root, singular PascalCase (for example Order, Invoice, Reservation).

aggregateLower.description: Lower-case aggregate name: local variables, route segments, and resource-string prose.

title.description: Name of the aggregate's main text property, singular PascalCase (for example Name, Subject, CustomerName). Everything that names it moves with it: the domain property and its invariant, the error codes (<aggregate>.<Title>.Empty and .TooLong), the <Title>MaxLength constant, the DTO and request properties, the EF column, the FluentValidation rule, the UI field and column resource entries, the typed API client, and the domain tests. No fileRename: no file in the seed is named after it.

titleCamel.description: Camel-case form of the main text property: factory and method parameters, private fields, named arguments, and nameof() targets. firstLowerCase (not lowerCase) is what keeps a multi-word value a valid camel-case identifier: CustomerName -> customerName, not customername. The price is that a plain substring replacement also reaches ENGLISH PROSE, so the two shipped error messages read "cannot be empty" against the camel-case spelling for a multi-word value. Deliberate trade-off: identifiers have to compile, and the two strings are a one-line edit in the module's error resources after generating.

child.description: Name of the aggregate's child entity, singular PascalCase. The generated type is <aggregate><child>, so --aggregate Order --child Item produces OrderItem with AddItem / EditItem / RemoveItem slices and /items routes. IGNORED when --flat is passed, which drops the child collection entirely.

childLower.description: Lower-case child name: local variables, parameter names, and prose.

childPlural.description: Plural child name: the navigation collection, the DbSet, and the use-case folder names. Derived by an English pluralizer (Item -> Items, Entry -> Entries, Box -> Boxes); rename by hand if your noun is irregular.

childPluralLower.description: Lower-case plural child name: the REST route segment and prose.

eventVerb.description: Verb naming the creation integration event, past tense PascalCase (for example Created, Placed, Booked). The generated event is <aggregate><EventVerb>IntegrationEvent and its consumer <aggregate><EventVerb>Handler, so --aggregate Order --event-verb Placed produces OrderPlacedIntegrationEvent and OrderPlacedHandler. The id is database-generated, so this event is published AFTER the commit by the create handler rather than raised as a domain event by the factory.

eventVerbLower.description: Lower-case verb: the prose that has to follow the event name rather than sit beside it, in the event's XML doc, the consumer's log message, and the UI success resource entry.

flat.description: Generate the module WITHOUT a child collection: no child entity, DTO, requests, mapper, EF configuration, Add/Edit/Remove slices, controller endpoints, identifier alias, or tests. Use it when your aggregate owns no growable children. Makes --child irrelevant.

noStatus.description: Generate the module WITHOUT a status axis: no status enum, no ChangeStatus slice, request, or endpoint, no Status property, and no status invariant or tests. Use it when your aggregate has no lifecycle state.

noDescription.description: Generate the module WITHOUT the aggregate's long-text property: no Description property or invariant, no <Description>MaxLength constant, no DTO, request, or command field, no validator rule, no EF max-length configuration, no error-resource entries, no UI field, and no tests for it. Use it when the aggregate's main text property is all the text it needs.

noOwner.description: Generate the module WITHOUT the aggregate's owning-user property: no RequesterUserId property, no create-request field or validator rule, no member on the creation integration event, no EF index, no UI field or column, and no tests for it. Use it when the aggregate is not owned by a single user, or until you add an Identity module to resolve one.

choices.description: SQL Server. The Aspire AppHost declares a container and a database resource, entity configurations inherit EntityTypeConfigurationSQLServer, and the migrations project targets Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer.

SQLite. A single file, no container and no server: entity configurations inherit EntityTypeConfigurationSqlite, the migrations project targets Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite and is named .Migrations.Sqlite.<Module>, and the app is single-tenant (the database-per-tenant demo needs a second server-backed database).

database.description: Relational engine for the sample module. Both shapes are the same application code: the engine is a configuration-base choice plus a connection string, which is the whole point of the framework's data-source routing.

engineName.description: Pascal spelling of the engine (SqlServer / Sqlite). It is what renames the migrations project (folder, csproj, namespace, assembly, and every reference to it), the two engine provider package ids, and the design-time helper call DesignTimeDbContextHelper.CreateSqlServer -> CreateSqlite. DERIVED from --database; there is no flag of its own.

engineNameUpper.description: The framework's OTHER spelling of the same engine (SQLServer / Sqlite), which is the one its public types and settings use. It renames the design-time factory (file and class), SQLServerDbContext -> SqliteDbContext, EntityTypeConfigurationSQLServer -> EntityTypeConfigurationSqlite, and the SQLServerConnectionString / SQLServerMigrationsAssembly settings properties. Two symbols rather than one because the two spellings are both real: renaming either alone leaves half the tree pointing at the other engine.

noAspire.description: Generate the solution WITHOUT the Aspire AppHost: no orchestration project, no Aspire.Hosting.* pins, and the UI host reaches the API through a fixed localhost address instead of service discovery. The hosts keep AddServiceDefaults() (telemetry, health endpoints, resilience) either way, so adding an AppHost later is additive. Run the two hosts yourself: dotnet run the API host, then the UI host.

frameworkVersion.description: The MMCA.Common package version to pin. Every MMCA.Common.* entry moves together (ADR-016); there is no phased rollout and no version skew across the set. Both values here are DERIVED: build/templates/stage.ps1 re-stamps them from the seed's own Directory.Packages.props, so a framework bump does not have to remember to touch this file.

localMmca.description: Emit a local.props that builds against ../MMCA.Common/Source via ProjectReference instead of consuming the published nuget.org packages. Use this only when the app sits beside the framework source in the same workspace.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic restore after the solution is created.

modifiers.comment: The analyzer baseline is copied verbatim. It carries no scaffold token, and its rule descriptions contain the words this template renames (comment, ticket), which substring replacement would otherwise mangle. build/templates/stage.ps1 rewrites its seed-specific header and appends the scaffold delta, and guards that both happened.

Two one-element razor wrappers, copied verbatim for the same reason as the .editorconfig and with the opposite ownership: everything else in the UI host is the adopter's to rename, these two exist so the UI host has NO occurrence left of two framework spellings that --title would mangle. PageHeading wraps the browser-tab element, whose tag name ends in the very word --title replaces; SectionHeading wraps the MudBlazor typography member spelled sub + that same word, which is an enum member and cannot be respelled. Razor markup has no per-occurrence escape form (the .resx trick of an XML character reference has no equivalent), so isolating each spelling in a file that is never processed is the whole mechanism. Both files must therefore stay free of every seed token; build/templates/stage.ps1 asserts that, and that this declaration still exists.

The wire-up script, copied verbatim for a third reason. It is a script ABOUT this scaffold: it shells out to dotnet new mmca-module and passes the flags through by name, so replacement would rewrite --title / --event-verb / --child into the adopter's own values and produce a script calling dotnet new with arguments no template declares. Shipping it unprocessed is the only working form. The price is that it can rely on no seed name being fixed up either, which is why it discovers the solution file, the app namespace, the existing module, and the host and test project paths at run time; build/templates/stage.ps1 asserts it names none of them and that this declaration still exists.
--flat: the whole child (comment) axis, file by file. Partial-file removals are marker regions in the seed that stage.ps1 turns into conditional directives.
--no-status: the whole status axis, file by file.

The seed's migrations describe the FULL sample schema (child table, status column, description column, requester column and its index) against SQL Server. Any shape flag makes them wrong on arrival, and --database sqlite makes them wrong for a second reason (they are SQL Server DDL, and their model snapshot names SQLServerDbContext), so they are dropped and the adopter runs 'dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate' against the shape they asked for. Migrations/.editorconfig still ships: dotnet ef never recreates it.

--database sqlite: the API host's appsettings.json differs structurally rather than by one value (a different connection-string key, a different migrations-assembly key, a DataSources entry, and no database-per-tenant override), and .json carries no marker regions in this seed. The sqlite copy ships beside it from build/templates/overlay and is renamed into place; the SQL Server copy comes out. Paths here are SOURCE paths, matched before any rename.

--no-aspire: the orchestration project, and the two files that assume it. The UI host resolves the API as 'https+http://web' through Aspire service discovery; standalone it needs the API host's own dev address, which is fixed in that host's launchSettings.json. The README is the other one: it is prose about running the app, and prose has no conditional form.

postActions.description: Restore NuGet packages required by this solution.
